{"draft": "ConocoPhillips earnings climb in second quarter on higher prices
ConocoPhillips reported second-quarter 2026 earnings of $3.9 billion, or $3.23 per share, compared with $2.0 billion, or $1.56 per share in the same period a year earlier.
Excluding special items, the company posted adjusted earnings of $4.0 billion, or $3.24 per share, up from $1.8 billion, or $1.42 per share a year earlier. The increase was driven primarily by higher prices, with its total average realized price rising to $62.33 per BOE, 36% higher than the $45.77 per BOE realized a year earlier.
Production came to 2,248 MBOED in the quarter. After adjusting for closed acquisitions and dispositions, production slipped 98 MBOED, or 4%, from a year earlier, while Lower 48 production reached 1,479 MBOED.
Cash provided by operating activities was $7.4 billion, and cash from operations excluding a change in working capital was $7.2 billion. The company funded $3.0 billion of capital expenditures and investments, repurchased $2.0 billion of shares and paid $1.0 billion in ordinary dividends.
The company declared a third-quarter ordinary dividend of $0.84 per share and expects third-quarter production of 2.29 to 2.32 million barrels of oil equivalent per day. It also signed agreements to sell noncore Lower 48 assets for $1.7 billion and lifted its total LNG offtake to 12 MTPA."}
